questions.question: Of the given four options, choose the one sentence that has no errors.

options.text: The class was very quiet when the teacher was giving a lecture.
The school principle refused to give permission to attend the match.
My boss complemented me on my work performance.
The sight of the animals being killed by poachers was a crime indeed.

questions.solution:
First sentence: **when **should be replaced with **while.**

Second sentence: A **principal **is the head of the school, not 'principle'.

Third sentence: The error in the sentence lies in the use of the word 'complement' which means 'to add to or make complete'. The correct word here should be '**compliment**' which means 'to praise (someone) for something'.

Only the fourth sentence is error free.

Hence, the correct answer is **option 4.**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

OUTSTANDING
questions.solution:
Here are the meanings of some of the given options:

 
• **Outstanding**: very good, excellent
 
• **Arrogant**: behaving in an unpleasant way
 
• **Wonderful** also means something very good and pleasant.
 
• **Ordinary **is nothing great or just normal.

Clearly, **ordinary **is opposite in meaning to the given word. 

Hence, **option 4 is correct.**

questions.question:
**Which one of the following options is the right form of the sentence which has been framed using the given parts?**

Three years/ in Greece / has been / the past / for Sujoy / working

options.text: Three years in Greece Sujoy has been working for the past.
Sujoy has been working in Greece for the past three years.
Sujoy in the past three years has been for working Greece.
Sujoy in the past three years in Greece has been working.

questions.solution:
The correct **option is 2 **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dbd70ea3a020b879b11334d2851ddd8dbc9b8a39e2f5af5675278c35a1f54f8d.png] Explanation-**

 
• The sentence structure in English follows the **subject+ verb+ object** word order.
 
• Here, **Sujoy **is the subject and **has been working** is the verb. The rest is additional information.

So the right form of the sentence is:***Sujoy has been working in Greece for the past three years.***

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

People build __different__ types of houses for living.
questions.solution:
Here are the meanings of the given words:

 
• **Different** means not the same. 
 
• **Changing **means making or becoming different.
 
• **Contrasting** also means different.
 
• **Distinct **means recognizably different in nature from something else of a similar type
 
• **Similar**: like something or somebody

 

Clearly, **similar **is completely opposite in meaning to the word **different. **

Hence, **option 4 is correct.**

 

Note: The other given options are synonyms of the word **different.**

questions.question:
**Choose the option that can be substituted for the given phrase.**

Action of reviewing past events in one’s life
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words in the options are:

• **Reflection**: a careful thought about something

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most suitable word.

A teacher who teaches younger children should have _________ patience.
questions.solution:
We know that a lot of patience is needed to teach younger children.

Hence**, infinite** is the correct word that can fit in the blank. Therefore, **option 3 is correct.**

 
• **Infinite **means never-ending (quantity).
 
• **Inclusive **means containing (a specified element) as part of a whole.
 
• **Indefinite **means lasting for an unknown or unstated length of time.
 
• **Independent **means free from outside control; not subject to another's authority.

questions.solution:

• **Attentive**: listening or watching carefully and with interest
 
• **Careful**: giving attention 

 

Clearly, **Competent** is the most appropriate synonym for the word **Efficient.**

questions.question:
**Choose the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence:**

The __traditional__ approach to teaching is not very effective today.
questions.solution:
The meanings of the given words are as follows.

 
• **Traditional: **being part of beliefs and customs of a particular group of people.
 
• **Modern: **of the present time or recent times
 
• **Outmoded: **no longer fashionable or useful
 
• **Neo-classical: **used to describe art and architecture that is based on the style of ancient Greece or Rome
 
• **Conventional: **tending to follow what is done or considered acceptable by society in general

 

It is clear that **modern** is the most appropriate antonym for the given word **traditional**.

Hence, **option 1 is correct.**

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence:

I had a __fleeting__ moment of panic but I recovered quickly.
questions.solution:
The meanings of the given words are as follows.

 
• **Fleeting**: lasting only a short time
 
• **Flaring**: to suddenly start or become much stronger
 
• **Brief**: lasting only a short time
 
• **Durable**: last for a long time 
 
• **Definite**: sure or certain

 

It is clear that **brief** is the most appropriate synonym for **fleeting**.

Hence, **option 2 is correct.**

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The given sentence means “All schools will be closed for the next three days **because of** heavy rains.”

Out of the given options, only '**on account of**’ means **‘because of’**.

Hence, **option 4** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Four parts of the following sentence have been underlined. Select the part that is INCORRECT.

The past of __man have been on the whole__ a pretty __beastly business__, a business of fighting, __bullying__ __and__ __hurting__.
questions.solution:
The error in the sentence lies in the usage of the verb 'have'. 

The correct form should be** has. **This is because the singular verb **has** should be used with the singular subject **the past of man**.

Hence, **option 3 is correct.**

__Correct sentence: __

The past of man **has **been on the whole a pretty beastly business, a business of fighting, bullying and hurting.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

SPONTANEOUS
questions.solution:
The meanings of the given words are as follows:

 
• **Spontaneous: **happening naturally, without being made to happen
 
• **Concurrent: ** existing or happening at the same time
 
• **Artful: **designed or done in a clever way
 
• **Impulsive: **acting suddenly without thinking carefully
 
• **Planned: **to make detailed arrangements 

 

It is clear that **Impulsive** is the most appropriate synonym for **Spontaneous**.

Hence, **option 3 is correct.**

questions.question:
Choose the option which can be used to explain a trait of Ravi’s based on the first sentence.

Ravi talks a lot to explain something very trivial. He is _____.
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words in the options are:

 
• **Garrulous: **talking a lot, especially about unimportant things
 
• **Friendly: **behaving in a kind and pleasant way 
 
• **Banal: **very ordinary
 
• **Pragmatic: **solving problems in a practical and sensible way.

 

**Garrulous** can correctly explain the described trait of Ravi, ie. that 'he talks a lot'. 

Hence, **option 1 is correct. **

questions.question: **Of the given four options, choose the one sentence that has no errors.**

options.text: We should not trespass private grounds.
Today Chinese possess many strategies that may improve their yield.
Sam was very noticeable in his class his friendly behavior endeared him to others.
The app was devised in such a way that it could self-destruct on its own within a particular period of time.

questions.solution:
**Option 4 **is the correct answer.

 
• First sentence: The verb** trespass **is always followed by the preposition **on**.
 
• Second sentence: There should be a **comma** after today in the second sentence.
 
• Third sentence: There should be a **conjunction** like **and **to combine the two clauses.

 

There are no errors in the fourth sentence and it is therefore the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Fill in the blank with the most suitable words.**

I am not going to _____ the haphazard working style of my maid servant.
questions.solution:
**Haphazard** means **unorganized**.

The meanings of the words given in the options are:

 
• **Cope with: **to deal successfully with something difficult
 
• **Put down: **to stop holding something
 
• **Put on with: **to put clothes or shoes onto your body
 
• **Put up with: **to accept somebody/something that is annoying, unpleasant, etc.

 

A **haphazard **working style is very unpleasant. So, based on the meanings of the phrases, **put up with **is the right fit in the blank.

Hence, **option 4 is correct.**

questions.question: What, according to the author, was one of the most irritating problems of travelling?

options.text: Carrying a lighter luggage with less space for things.
Carrying a lighter luggage but still wanting enough space for things.
Not having to check in one’s luggage.

questions.solution:
The part of the passage that states “*one of your most vexing travel problems: **being able to pack light** enough on an outbound flight to avoid checking luggage, **but having adequate room** on the return for all the goods acquired on your journey*” gives the answer.

Hence, **option 2 is correct.**

questions.question: What is NOT the unique feature of the product described in the passage?

options.text: It is light enough to be carried in the flight
It is a famous brand product and is of good quality
It expands double in size and the side walls are still rigid
It is the most preferred brand product among travelers

questions.solution:
Options 1,2 and 3 mention the various unique features of the given product whereas the fourth one is clearly not mentioned as a feature of the product in the passage.

Hence, **option 4 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: What is the main idea of this passage?

options.text: Describing the problems in air travel.

questions.solution:
In the passage, “*The line goes on sale next month: Plan your itineraries accordingly.*” suggests that the passage promotes sales of a particular product.

Hence, **option 2 is correct.**

questions.question: What does the author mean by the phrase ‘a suitcase that’ll outwit even the most reckless baggage hander'?

options.text: A smart suitcase that can be easily handled by any baggage handler.
A suitcase that can be easily handled by the most irresponsible baggage handler.
A suitcase that would fare better even when handled by the most careless baggage handler.
A suitcase that is smarter than the most casual baggage handler.

questions.solution:
**Outwit** means to defeat somebody/something.

**Reckless** means showing a lack of care.

So, the phrase means ‘a suitcase that would be able to survive even when handled carelessly’.

**Hence, option 3 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: What does the word ‘faceted’ mean as per the passage?
questions.solution:
**Facet** means a particular part, feature or aspect of something

Hence,** featured** means the same as **faceted**.

Therefore, **option 3 is correct.**

questions.question:
Four parts of the following sentence have been underlined. Select the part that is INCORRECT.

__According to scientists__, the earth was first a globe of highly heated gas, __then it became__ liquid and __with__ __further cooling__ a crust formed __in the liquid interior.__
questions.solution:
The error in the sentence is in the last part ie. the phrase 'liquid interior' is ungrammatical.

__Correction__**: ‘in the interior of the liquid’** would be the correct phrase to be used in the place of **‘in the liquid interior’**.

Hence, **option 1 is the right answer.**
